heading_en: Risk Factors for Delta Risk, Vega Risk and Curvature Risk
summary_ja: 一般金利・信用スプレッド（非証券化、非CTP、CTP）・株式・コモディティ・外国為替の各リスクについて、デルタ・ベガ・カーベチャー各リスクのリスク・ファクターの設定要件を定める。
summary_en: Sets the requirements for specifying risk factors for delta, vega and curvature risk for general interest rate, credit spread (non-securitization, non-CTP and CTP), equity, commodity and foreign exchange risk.
paragraphs: The risk factors for general interest rate risk shall be set as provided in the following items according to the category of risk listed in each item. (i) Delta risk: to be set as provided in (a) through (c) according to the category of curve listed in (a) through (c): (a) The risk-free yield curve of each currency: all of the following requirements shall be satisfied: (1) In each currency, at least one curve shall be set based on the market-implied swap curve used to mark to market the money market instrument or position with the lowest credit risk that is subject to measurement of the market risk equivalent amount; (2) The tenors of the risk-free yield curve of each currency shall be 0.25 years, 0.5 years, 1 year, 2 years, 3 years, 5 years, 10 years, 15 years, 20 years and 30 years; (3) Where a curve created using market data on bonds issued by a central government is to be substituted for the risk-free yield curve, this shall be limited to cases where data on the market-implied swap curve are insufficient. In this case, where there are bonds issued by the central governments of multiple countries within the area of the same currency, an appropriate central government representing the risk of that area shall be chosen; (4) Where a swap curve is applied to sensitivities determined from bonds for general interest rate risk, the basis risk between the bond curve and the credit default swap curve shall be captured in the credit spread risk class; (5) In constructing the risk-free yield curve of each currency, in the case of the following combinations of curves, the curves in that combination shall be set as different curves: (i) the overnight index swap (OIS) curve and the interbank offered rate (BOR) swap curve; (ii) multiple interbank offered rate (BOR) curves with different tenors; (iii) onshore market and offshore market curves; (b) The flat curve of the inflation rate in the market of each currency: all of the following requirements shall be satisfied: (1) The term structure of the yield curve shall not be recognized; (2) The sensitivity to the inflation rate shall be calculated from the implied coupon of inflation instruments (meaning instruments whose cash flows are linked to an inflation index; the same applies hereinafter in this (2) and (3)) (meaning the expected interest rate of that instrument back-calculated from prices observed in the inflation instrument market), and the inflation risk (meaning the risk that the price of a held instrument falls due to price changes; the same applies hereinafter in this paragraph) of each currency shall be aggregated; (3) The inflation rate risk factor shall be included only in inflation instruments, and risk factors for general interest rate risk other than inflation risk shall be included in the instruments subject to inflation risk; (4) Inflation risk shall be allocated to the term structure of the relevant risk-free yield curve of the same currency; (c) The flat curve of the cross-currency basis of each currency (excluding the pivot currency (meaning one currency set by the Ultimate Designated Parent Company, being the currency of the United States of America (USD) or the currency of the participating countries of the European Economic and Monetary Union (EUR); the same applies hereinafter in this (c))): all of the following requirements shall be satisfied: (1) The term structure of the yield curve shall not be recognized; (2) The cross-currency basis shall be the basis against the pivot currency; (3) A cross-currency basis not involving the pivot currency shall be set by combining cross-currency bases against the pivot currency; (4) In addition to the sensitivity of the same instrument to general interest rate risk, cross-currency basis risk shall be included. In this case, cross-currency basis risk shall be allocated to the term structure of the relevant risk-free yield curve of the same currency; (ii) Vega risk: to be set so as to satisfy all of the following requirements: (a) In each currency, the implied volatility of options referencing underlying assets that have sensitivity to general interest rate risk shall be set as a risk factor; (b) With respect to the maturity of the option, the implied volatility of the option shall be associated with one of one or more tenors (0.5 years, 1 year, 3 years, 5 years or 10 years); (c) With respect to the residual maturity of the underlying asset of the option as of the expiry date of the option's exercise period, the implied volatility of the option shall be associated with one of one or more tenors of residual maturity up to maturity (0.5 years, 1 year, 3 years, 5 years or 10 years); (d) Where a swap curve is applied to sensitivities determined from bonds for general interest rate risk, the basis risk between the bond curve and the credit default swap curve shall be captured in the credit spread risk class; (iii) Curvature risk: to be set so as to satisfy all of the following requirements: (a) It shall be calculated by a parallel shift of the risk-free yield curve of each currency; (b) Inflation risk and cross-currency basis risk shall be excluded from the measurement of curvature risk; (c) Where a swap curve is applied to sensitivities determined from bonds for general interest rate risk, the basis risk between the bond curve and the credit default swap curve shall be captured in the credit spread risk class.

The risk factors for credit spread risk relating to non-securitization products shall be set as provided in the following items according to the category of risk listed in each item. (i) Delta risk: to be set so as to satisfy all of the following requirements: (a) They shall be determined according to the characteristics of the issuer's credit spread curve relating to bonds and credit default swaps; (b) They shall be determined according to tenors (0.5 years, 1 year, 3 years, 5 years or 10 years); (ii) Vega risk: to be set so as to satisfy all of the following requirements: (a) It shall be the implied volatility of options referencing, as underlying assets, issues of issuers relating to bonds and credit default swaps; (b) With respect to the maturity of the option, the implied volatility shall be associated with the maturity (0.5 years, 1 year, 3 years, 5 years or 10 years); (iii) Curvature risk: calculated by a parallel shift of all tenors set on the issuer's credit spread curve relating to bonds and credit default swaps.

The risk factors for credit spread risk relating to securitization products (non-CTP) shall be set as provided in the following items according to the category of risk listed in each item. (i) Delta risk: to be set so as to satisfy all of the following requirements: (a) It shall be the spread of the tranche held, not the spread of the underlying assets of that securitization product (non-CTP); (b) It shall be based on the characteristics of the tranche's credit spread curve; (c) It shall be based on tenors (0.5 years, 1 year, 3 years, 5 years or 10 years); (ii) Vega risk: to be set so as to satisfy all of the following requirements: (a) It shall be the implied volatility of options referencing securitization products (non-CTP) as underlying assets; (b) With respect to the maturity of the option, the implied volatility shall be associated with the maturity (0.5 years, 1 year, 3 years, 5 years or 10 years); (iii) Curvature risk: calculated by a parallel shift of all tenors set on the credit spread curve of the tranche held.

The risk factors for credit spread risk relating to securitization products (CTP) shall be set as provided in the items below (excluding item (ii) for tranches whose implied volatility cannot be obtained) according to the category of risk listed in each item. (i) Delta risk: to be set so as to satisfy all of the following requirements: (a) It shall be with respect to the issues of the underlying assets of the securitization product or nth-to-default products; (b) It shall be determined according to the characteristics of the credit spread curve of the underlying assets held; (c) It shall be based on tenors (0.5 years, 1 year, 3 years, 5 years or 10 years); (ii) Vega risk: to be set so as to satisfy all of the following requirements: (a) It shall be the implied volatility of options referencing securitization products (CTP) as underlying assets; (b) With respect to the maturity of the option, the implied volatility shall be associated with the maturity (0.5 years, 1 year, 3 years, 5 years or 10 years); (iii) Curvature risk: calculated by a parallel shift of all tenors set on the credit spread curve of the tranche held.

The risk factors for equity risk shall be set as provided in the following items according to the category of risk listed in each item. (i) Delta risk: the spot prices of equities, etc. and the equity repo rates, etc. (including dividend yield; the same applies hereinafter) shall be taken into account; (ii) Vega risk: to be set so as to satisfy all of the following requirements: (a) It shall be the implied volatility of options referencing the spot price of equities, etc. as underlying assets; (b) With respect to the maturity of the option, the implied volatility shall be associated with the maturity (0.5 years, 1 year, 3 years, 5 years or 10 years); (c) Equity repo rates, etc. shall not be included in the vega risk factors; (iii) Curvature risk: to be set with respect to the spot price of equities, etc. In this case, equity repo rates, etc. shall not be included in the curvature risk factors.

The risk factors for commodity risk shall be set as provided in the following items according to the category of risk listed in each item. (i) Delta risk: it shall be the spot price of the commodity and shall be set so as to satisfy all of the following requirements; provided, however, that for commodities traded more frequently at futures prices than at spot prices, futures prices may be used for the relevant risk factor: (a) It shall be determined taking into account the delivery location included in the trading terms of the commodity; (b) It shall be based on the remaining period to maturity (0 years, 0.25 years, 0.5 years, 1 year, 2 years, 3 years, 5 years, 10 years, 15 years, 20 years or 30 years); (ii) Vega risk: to be set so as to satisfy all of the following requirements: (a) It shall be the implied volatility of options referencing the spot price of the commodity as the underlying asset; (b) It shall not be required to distinguish the spot price of the commodity according to the maturity or delivery location of the underlying asset; (c) With respect to the maturity of the option, the implied volatility shall be associated with the maturity (0.5 years, 1 year, 3 years, 5 years or 10 years); (iii) Curvature risk: calculated by a parallel shift of all tenors set on the spot price of each commodity.

The risk factors for foreign exchange risk shall be set as provided in the following items according to the category of risk listed in each item. In this case, it shall not be required to treat onshore or offshore of the same exchange rate as different exchange rates. (i) Delta risk: to be set so as to satisfy all of the following requirements: (a) They shall be set using all exchange rates between the currency of the instrument and the reporting currency; provided, however, that in the case of a transaction referencing exchange rates between currencies other than the reporting currency, the foreign exchange delta risk factors shall be set using all exchange rates between the reporting currency and the currencies other than the reporting currency; (b) Where the base currency approach (meaning an approach, notified to the Commissioner of the Financial Services Agency, of using a currency other than the reporting currency (hereinafter in this Article and Article 261-3, paragraph (1), item (vi) referred to as the "base currency") in place of the reporting currency; the same applies hereinafter in this Article) is used, all of the following requirements shall be satisfied: (1) The base currency shall be a single currency; (2) By calculating foreign exchange risk against the base currency, it shall appropriately represent the risk of its own portfolio, and it shall be able to explain its consideration of translation risk between the base currency and the reporting currency; (3) The market risk equivalent amount shall be calculated including the following foreign exchange risks: (i) foreign exchange risk against the base currency; (ii) foreign exchange risk between the reporting currency and the base currency; (4) Foreign exchange risk under the base currency approach shall be converted into the market risk equivalent amount in the reporting currency using the spot exchange rate as of the calculation reference date that reflects foreign exchange risk between the base currency and the reporting currency; (ii) Vega risk: to be set so as to satisfy all of the following requirements: (a) It shall be the implied volatility of options referencing exchange rates; (b) With respect to the maturity of the option, the implied volatility shall be associated with the maturity (0.5 years, 1 year, 3 years, 5 years or 10 years); (iii) Curvature risk: to be set so as to satisfy all of the following requirements: (a) They shall be identified using all exchange rates between the currency of the instrument and the reporting currency; provided, however, that in the case of a transaction referencing exchange rates between currencies other than the reporting currency, they shall be identified using all exchange rates between the following currencies: (1) The reporting currency; (2) The currency of the instrument and the currencies other than that currency referenced by the instrument; (b) Foreign exchange risk under the base currency approach shall be converted into the market risk equivalent amount in the reporting currency using the spot exchange rate as of the calculation reference date that reflects foreign exchange risk between the base currency and the reporting currency.
